questions.stem: A flow that has run for months starts failing on an Okta "Add User to Group" action with a permissions error. Nothing in the flow changed. What is the most likely cause?
options: The flow exceeded its 30-day execution history
The group was renamed
The Okta connection's scopes or the authorising account's role changed, and the connection needs reauthorising
The Workflows Console session expired
questions.explanation: The Okta connection carries OAuth scopes and acts as a specific account. If scopes were customised, Okta added a scope the card needs, or the account lost super admin, actions fail with authorisation errors until the connection is reauthorised. The flow itself gives no hint of this.

questions.stem: You want a flow to fire only when a user is added to the "contractors" group. Where does that filter go?
options: In a Continue If (or similar branching) card immediately after the event card
On the event card itself, as a group selector you assume exists
In the flow's folder settings
In the Slack card's recipient field
questions.explanation: Do not rely on the event card to select the group. Inspect the group name output yourself and stop early with a branching card. Filtering first keeps executions cheap and the history readable.

questions.stem: After switching a flow on, you add a test user to the group and see no execution for several seconds. Which is NOT a plausible explanation?
options: The flow is actually still off
The Okta connection is unauthorised
Event delivery is asynchronous and the execution has not arrived yet
Execution History has reached its 30-day retention and stopped recording
questions.explanation: Retention is a rolling window: old executions drop off, new ones are always recorded. The other three are the standard causes of a silent flow. Check the toggle, check the connection, then wait a little longer before assuming a bug.

questions.stem: In Execution History the Compose card's output reads "User undefined was added to contractors". What went wrong?
options: Execution History truncates long values
The mapping into the Compose card points at an empty or wrong event output field
The user had no login attribute in Okta
The Slack connection lacks the correct scope
questions.explanation: History shows exactly what each card received. "undefined" in a composed string means the mapped source field was empty for that run, almost always because the wrong output was dragged in. Open the event card's outputs in the same execution to see which fields actually carried data.

questions.stem: Why does Okta recommend authorising the Okta connection with a dedicated service account rather than your own admin login?
options: Service accounts get higher rate limits
Service accounts do not need scopes
Actions through the connection are attributed to the authorising account, so your name would appear on every automated change
Personal accounts cannot hold super admin
questions.explanation: The connection is the identity the flow acts as. With a dedicated account, System Log clearly separates human changes from automation, and the connection does not break when an individual admin leaves or loses their role. Rate limits and scopes are unaffected.
